title: The Factory That Used Prison Labor to Make 'Artisan' Bread—for $0.15 an Hour
hook: Listen to this: a premium bakery chain was using prison inmates to bake their ‘handcrafted’ loaves, paying pennies while selling them for $8.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines the rage against corporate exploitation with a shocking disconnect between the 'artisan' branding and the grim reality.

title: The CEO Who Bought a Small Town—Then Banned the Internet
hook: Imagine a CEO purchasing an entire town, then forbidding any internet access so residents could only buy from his stores.
why_this_can_go_viral: The dystopian premise of a modern feudal lord is instantly shareable, triggering fear and fascination.

title: The Startup That Faked a Million Users—With 10 Employees and a Bot Farm
hook: A startup raised $50 million by showing investors a dashboard of 'active users' that were actually a spreadsheet and 500 sock puppets.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exposes the 'fake it till you make it' culture at its most criminal, appealing to anyone suspicious of tech hype.

title: The 'Freemium' Game That Psychologically Destroyed Its Youngest Players
hook: A top mobile game used a hidden algorithm to detect children's emotional lows and then sell them 'boosts' until they cried or spent $500.
why_this_can_go_viral: The combination of children, addiction, and psychological warfare is highly emotive and shareable among parents and gamers.

title: The Corporate Spy Who Infiltrated a Competitor's Holiday Party—and Stole the Company
hook: A rival executive attended a competitor's Christmas party as a temp bartender and walked out with the entire client list on his phone.
why_this_can_go_viral: A relatable, almost cinematic story that feels like a heist movie, easy to visualize and retell.

title: The Industry Cover-Up of 'Waterproof' Makeup—It Was Dissolving Your Eyelids
hook: A major cosmetics brand silently reformulated their 'waterproof' mascara to use a glue that caused chronic eyelid inflammation—and hid the lawsuits.
why_this_can_go_viral: Appeals directly to the huge beauty audience, who will immediately question the products on their faces.

title: The Trader Who Used a Fake 'CEO Suicide' Call to Sink a Rival's Stock
hook: A trader made a single phone call to a news wire, pretending to be a grieving assistant, and wiped $2 billion off a competitor's market cap.
why_this_can_go_viral: Demonstrates the terrifying fragility of financial markets, combining the shock of a death hoax with massive financial loss.

title: The 'Green' Energy Startup That Was Just a Diesel Generator in a Shed
hook: Investors thought they were funding solar panels—the truth was a hidden diesel generator that ran 24/7 to make the 'green' numbers look good.
why_this_can_go_viral: Taps into the growing skepticism around 'green' investing and ESG scams, with a beautifully simple, absurd visual.

title: The Cartel That Controlled the Global Avocado Market—by Threatening Farmers' Families
hook: A single cartel didn't just smuggle avocados—they forced every farmer in a region to sell at their price, or their children would disappear.
why_this_can_go_viral: Connects a beloved consumer product (guacamole) with a terrifying criminal underworld, creating a high shock factor.

title: The HR Firm That Used a 'Voodoo' Algorithm to Decide Who Gets Fired
hook: A major HR software company secretly included a 'jinx' factor: if an employee’s name appeared in a negative Slack message, the algorithm flagged them for layoffs.
why_this_can_go_viral: Everyone fears being laid off by a cold algorithm; this story confirms those fears are justified.

title: The 'Ethical' Fast Fashion Brand That Was Just a Money Laundering Front
hook: A popular 'sustainable' clothing line was actually a front for a drug cartel, shipping cocaine inside 'organic cotton' shirt packages.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines the trendy topic of ethical fashion with a shocking criminal twist, creating cognitive dissonance and high shareability.

title: The Industry Cover-Up of 'Silent' Dishwashers—They Were Just Deafeningly Loud, but Adjusted
hook: Every major appliance maker agreed to stop publishing decibel ratings for 'silent' dishwashers because the 'silent' models actually caused tinnitus.
why_this_can_go_viral: A relatable product complaint taken to a dark, conspiratorial level, appealing to homeowners and renters.

title: The Market Manipulator Who Used a Fake 'Shipping Forecast' to Corner the Coffee Market
hook: A trader bribed a radio station to broadcast a fake storm warning, stopping coffee shipments—then bought all the beans at a panic price.
why_this_can_go_viral: A delightful, old-school heist story that feels impossible, yet was real, with a universally loved product (coffee) at stake.

title: The Corporate Spy Who Infiltrated a Competitor by Faking a Paralysis
hook: A spy spent two years pretending to be a paraplegic to get hired as a remote accessibility tester—then copied the entire product roadmap.
why_this_can_go_viral: The extreme dedication and moral ambiguity of the spy make for a compelling, almost disturbing story.

title: The Dark Marketing Firm That Sold 'Calming' Apps to Parents—They Listened to Kids' Bedrooms
hook: A wellness app promised to 'track' a child's sleep—but the audio feed was being sold to advertisers to learn what families argued about.
why_this_can_go_viral: The ultimate violation of trust: turning a tool meant to protect children into a surveillance device for profit.

title: The CEO Who Used a 'Scientific' Personality Test to Deport Whistleblowers
hook: A CEO hired a fake psychologist to administer a 'personality test'—the real goal was to diagnose whistleblowers as 'mentally unstable' and have them deported.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exposes the weaponization of pseudoscience, a deeply unsettling abuse of power that feels systemic.

title: The Monopoly That Bought Every Public Park Bench—Then Charged You to Sit
hook: A single company bought the franchise rights for all park benches in a major city, then installed pay-per-minute kiosks on every seat.
why_this_can_go_viral: A dystopian, almost farcical example of privatization that everyone can instantly visualize and be outraged by.

title: The 'All-You-Can-Eat' Buffet That Used a Secret Ingredient to Make You Hungrier
hook: A buffet chain spiked their soup with a flavor enhancer that triggered hunger spikes 30 minutes later—making you buy the expensive dessert.
why_this_can_go_viral: Taps into the universal feeling of being tricked by a restaurant, with a specific, believable chemical twist.

title: The Startup Fraud That Sold 'Quantum Computers'—They Were Just Raspberry Pis in a Fancy Box
hook: A startup raised $100 million for a 'quantum cloud' service—the servers were just Raspberry Pi boards inside a custom aluminum case with LEDs.
why_this_can_go_viral: A perfect 'tech bro' scam that demystifies a complex topic with a hilarious, low-tech reveal.

title: The Industry Cover-Up of '5G-Safe' Masks—They Contained Conductive Metal Fibers
hook: A mask company claimed to block 5G radiation but secretly used conductive copper fibers that actually amplified radiation into the wearer’s brain.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines the controversial 5G topic with a terrifying 'cure is worse than the disease' angle.

title: The Market Manipulator Who Used a Fake 'Celebrity Endorsement' Tweet from 2015
hook: A trader hacked a forgotten, archived Twitter account of a dead celebrity, posted a stock tip, and cashed out before anyone realized the account was ancient.
why_this_can_go_viral: A clever, low-tech exploit that feels like a digital-age heist, easy to understand and share.

title: The Supply Chain Secret of 'Fresh' Sushi—It Was Frozen Over a Year Ago
hook: The sushi in your grocery store is not 'fresh'—it was caught, flash-frozen, and kept at -60°C for 18 months, then thawed and labeled 'fresh'.
why_this_can_go_viral: A shocking revelation for sushi lovers that changes how they see a common product, with high 'did you know?' factor.

title: The CEO Who Used a 'Loyalty' Program to Track and Fire Disgruntled Employees
hook: A CEO's 'employee wellness' app tracked how often you smiled at work—if your smile score dropped, you were flagged as 'toxic' and fired.
why_this_can_go_viral: A horrifying example of surveillance capitalism applied to the workplace, resonating deeply with remote and office workers.

title: The Corporate Spy Who Faked an Entire Company Subsidiary to Steal a Formula
hook: A spy created a fake company, registered a fake trademark, and hired a factory to make a fake product—all to get a sample of a rival's secret formula.
why_this_can_go_viral: The incredible complexity of the con makes for a fascinating, almost unbelievable story that rewards attention.

title: The Dark Marketing Campaign That Used Your Own Pet to Sell You Pet Insurance
hook: A pet insurance app scanned your dog's photos to detect 'health issues' and then sent you a targeted ad—even if your dog was perfectly healthy.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exploits the deep emotional bond people have with their pets, using fear to drive a purchase—a classic dark marketing tactic.
